figures.finding: A person attains full age in the Cayman Islands at eighteen (since 19 December 1977).
figures.applies: Age of Majority Act (1999 Revision) s. 2, legislation.gov.ky.

sources.said: 2. (1) As from 19th December, 1977, a person shall attain full age on attaining the age of eighteen instead of on attaining the age of twenty-one.

figures.finding: The Cayman Islands' Labour Act (2021 Revision) defines a child as a juvenile under fourteen and a juvenile as a person under seventeen, but sets no minimum age of employment in the text read: it forbids the worst forms of child labour (for those purposes a child is anyone under eighteen) and any other work the Cabinet prescribes as likely to harm a child's health, safety or morals (a reading of its silence; the Labour Act does not apply to the public service, charities or churches).
figures.applies: Labour Act (2021 Revision) ss. 2, 3, 80A, legislation.gov.ky (a newer Labour Act, if any, not checked).

sources.said: “child” means a juvenile under the age of fourteen years; ... “juvenile” means a person under the age of seventeen years; ... (f) subject to subsection (2), require a child to perform any other work prescribed which, by its nature or the circumstances in which it is carried out, is likely to harm the health, safety or morals of the child.

figures.finding: The Cayman Islands have no child-performer permit or hours rule in the Labour Act or the Children Act (2012 Revision, searched for employment and performance); the only bars are on using a child (under eighteen) for prostitution, pornography or pornographic performances and on prescribed harmful work, so the general law leaves a child's performing, writing or directing work unregulated (reading).
